_note: Math news for the home strip and /news (Nov 12, Jian). Newest items show on the home page; items older than about 2 months drop off the strip but stay on /news. Each url is the page the summary was written from. Summaries are our own words. Reputable sources only; nothing political or scary.

items.title: An AI proves a new piece of a famous prime number puzzle
items.why: The Riemann hypothesis, about how prime numbers are spread out, is still unsolved, but an AI proved a weaker version and mathematicians are now checking every step.

items.title: Google cuts errors 40 times in a key quantum computer step
items.why: Quantum computers need special ingredients called magic states, and Google showed a cheaper way to make them with far fewer mistakes.

items.title: Nobel Prize in Physics for catching ghost particles in Antarctic ice
items.why: Francis Halzen turned a cubic kilometer of South Pole ice into a giant detector for neutrinos, tiny particles that fly through Earth from deep space.

items.title: Four mathematicians win the 2026 Fields Medal
items.why: Hong Wang, one of the four, solved the Kakeya needle problem in 3D, a puzzle about turning a needle in every direction inside the smallest space.

items.title: Team USA takes second at the Math Olympiad with four golds
items.why: Six high school students went to Shanghai and came home with four gold medals, one silver and one bronze out of 117 teams.

items.title: Gerd Faltings wins the Abel Prize
items.why: He proved that a huge family of equations can only have a limited number of fraction answers, a puzzle that stumped mathematicians for 60 years.
